ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Yul Brynner — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Cycle 2 review: immune-related adverse event monitoring, symptoms, and return to work

text.paragraph: Mr. Brynner returns three weeks after his first pembrolizumab infusion, for cycle 2. He felt a little more tired for two days after the infusion and has otherwise felt well. He has had no diarrhea, abdominal pain, new cough or breathlessness, rash or itching, headache, dizziness, thirst, or yellowing. He saw the palliative care team two weeks ago and found the conversation about his goals and his worries useful; he is sleeping better. The injection medialization of his left vocal fold a week ago made his voice louder and less breathy, and he has begun light rehearsal with the voice therapist's exercises. He wants to rejoin the tour for a few performances a week next month. He has had no bone pain and has not smoked. His first zoledronic acid dose is today, with the pembrolizumab. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1983-10-13; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Louder and less breathy; longer phonation time
Slightly reduced breath sounds at the left apex; no crackles

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, stage IVB (cT4 N2 M1c, AJCC 8th edition), unresectable: the primary invades the mediastinum at the aortopulmonary window; bone metastases; PD-L1 tumor proportion score 70 percent (22C3); ECOG performance status 1; comprehensive genomic profiling results in the notes
S — Synthetic modern histology, stage, and biomarkers linked to his documented inoperable lung cancer of September 1983.
Bone metastases at T10, the right ilium, and the left sixth rib on PET-CT, without pain, fracture, or cord compression
S — Synthetic metastatic sites chosen so that first-line systemic therapy is the standard of care; no source describes the spread of his cancer.
Left vocal fold paralysis with a breathy, weak voice, most likely from left recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement by disease in the aortopulmonary window
S — Synthetic laryngoscopy finding anchored to the published account that a vocal-cord problem led to his diagnosis; the lay 'lump on his vocal cords' is not modeled as a laryngeal tumor.
Left upper lobe mass invading the mediastinum, with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, on CT at presentation; suspicious for lung cancer pending tissue diagnosis
S — Synthetic presenting imaging finding, recorded before the tissue diagnosis.
Former smoker: about 3 packs a day from age 12 until he quit 12 years ago, roughly 115 pack-years; no tobacco since
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to the documented heavy smoking and quitting; the pack-year figure is a synthetic midpoint of conflicting published amounts.

list.item:
Adenocarcinoma of the lung, stage IVB, on pembrolizumab (C34.12). Cycle 1 tolerated well. TSH 2.4 and free T4 1.1, liver tests, creatinine, and blood count normal; glucose 104 mg/dL on a mid-morning, non-fasting sample is not a concern. No immune-related adverse event. ESAS 12, down from 18; PHQ-9 4. [S]
Pembrolizumab cycle 2 today.
Laboratory panel before cycle 3; response CT about nine weeks after starting.
Once the first response scan is reviewed, consider pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks to fit the tour.

Bone metastases (C79.51). No pain; calcium 9.4 and eGFR 92; dental examination done. [S]
Zoledronic acid 4 mg today, then every 12 weeks.
Vitamin D3 1000 units daily and calcium from food.
Acetaminophen for aches after the first dose if needed.

Left vocal fold paralysis, after injection medialization (J38.01). Voice much improved. [S]
Continue voice therapy; graded return to performing as he chooses, with rest days between performances at first.

list.item: Tissue diagnosis, full staging, PD-L1, and comprehensive biomarker results before any systemic therapy, within three weeks of presentation. Outcome by 1983-09-22: Diagnosis and stage by two weeks; PD-L1 at two weeks and tissue sequencing at three weeks; pembrolizumab started the day the sequencing was reviewed [S]
First palliative care visit within eight weeks of diagnosis. Outcome by 1983-10-13: Seen by the palliative care team two weeks after diagnosis [S]
A voice strong enough for rehearsal by the second cycle. Outcome by 1983-10-13: Louder, less breathy voice one week after injection medialization; light rehearsal resumed with voice therapy [S]

No grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event missed: laboratory panel before each infusion and symptom review at each visit. Outcome by 1983-10-13: Panels normal before cycles 1 and 2; no symptoms of colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, or endocrine dysfunction [S]

Zoledronic acid started only after a dental examination and normal calcium and kidney function. Outcome by 1983-10-13: Dental examination three weeks earlier; calcium 9.4 and eGFR 92; first dose with cycle 2 [S]

Follow-up: Pembrolizumab cycle 2 and zoledronic acid today. Preventive visit in two weeks. Cycle 3 in three weeks with the laboratory panel. Response CT about nine weeks after starting. Next scheduled visit 1983-10-27: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
